about.title: Woodland Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Woodland's traffic runs through a mix of small-town streets and heavier state-route corridors, and that combination shows up in the numbers: 157 injury collisions and 199 injured people in the most recent reporting year, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. seeing the heaviest reported activity. Corridors like E Main Street, East Street, Main Street, and the I-5 corridor carry a lot of that volume. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the period right after matters — insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memory fades quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we're a free service that connects injured Woodland residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, handle communication with insurers, and help protect your right to recover compensation under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file suit in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like Yolo County or Caltrans — is involved. An attorney can flag that deadline early so it doesn't quietly pass.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces your payout. What you say to an insurance adjuster in a recorded statement can be used to shift more fault onto you, so it helps to have guidance before that call happens.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. An attorney working on contingency — no fee unless you recover — can help make sure those losses aren't undervalued by an insurer.

items.question: I was hurt near the I-5 and Main Street area — does it matter where the crash happened?
items.answer: Location can matter for evidence gathering, especially if the crash involved a state highway like I-5 or an intersection maintained by the city of Woodland. It can also affect which agency's records need to be pulled and whether a shorter government-claim deadline applies. An attorney can sort out these details quickly.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to find ways to shift fault onto you under California's comparative fault rules. A free consultation can help you understand what to say and what to avoid.

items.question: How much does it cost to work with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. This lets you get legal help without paying anything upfront while you focus on recovering.
